They pass the same SendTrace through judge(). The session-log send step (crates/sc-jev-check/src/run/log.rs) creates a fresh SendTrace per send. The tests that cover these paths pass, including crates/sc-jev-check/tests/session_log.rs and the wire tests. I found no integration defect between r-5 and r-6. This was a targeted read of those call sites, not a line-by-line review.

fenced_json.notes: I checked that the worktree HEAD resolves to sprint/r-6-session-log-record at b35a9c4cac9be7a3359e7e2597699664c596245a. The combined r-5 and r-6 code is consistent. sc-jev builds the body with CheckRequest::from_canonical(...).to_body() (check.rs:39-41). send_with_busy_retry's retry_loop records Sha256Digest::of_text(request.body()) into the SendTrace once per send, before the first transport send (retry.rs:420-422). So request_sha256 is the hash of the documented Jev body, and prompt_sha256 stays the canonical-payload digest. The engine creates a fresh SendTrace per backend send and emits exactly one SessionLogRow (log.rs:148-150). request_sha256 comes from trace.request_sha256() and is None if no body was built. model_id is judge.model_id(). The row goes out through LogEvent and row.to_fields(), with no bespoke writer. I did not re-run the std Mutex-across-await rule on a diff, because I had no shell and no diff. Neither retry.rs nor log.rs shows a lock held across an await. No findings are caused by combining r-5 and r-6.
